resources.string: Direct, end-to-end encrypted text between exactly two devices.
Pair once: one person creates an invitation code, the other joins with it. Afterwards the app reconnects on its own.
Partner label (stored on this device only)

Messages travel only over a direct, encrypted peer connection. Public DHT nodes, UDP trackers and STUN servers are used to help the two devices find each other; no server stores, forwards or reads chat content.

A direct connection cannot exist on every network (carrier-grade NAT, symmetric NAT, strict firewalls, some VPNs). There is no relay fallback, so the app reports failure instead of routing your messages through a third party.
The invitation is deleted from this device and you will have to pair again. Your local message history is kept.
Connected — direct on the local network
Direct connection unavailable on these networks. This is a network limitation, not a temporary glitch; the app will keep retrying but cannot use a relay.
The invitation code is a secret. Anyone who has it can try to connect to you, so share it only with the person you want to talk to, over a channel you trust.
Show this QR code to the other device, or copy the code and send it yourself.
